To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the angular resolution of GRAPES-2 was 1.0° at 30 TeV, 0.7 ± 0.2° at 100 TeV and 0.5° at 1 PeV.
the angular resolution of GRAPES-2 at 30 TeV is 0.7 ^{+0.3} −0.1 ° and that the angular resolution improves with increasing energy, reaching 0.2° at 10 PeV.
the GRAPES 3 EAS array has a 0.7 degree angular resolution at 30 TeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of the energy dependent angular resolutions and the absolute pointing accuracies of the GRAPEX-3 EAS detector array.
the angular resolution of the array, which is the most important parameter for the detection of point sources.
the study of the angular resolution of the array, and the measurement of the Moon and Sun shadow effect.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the angular resolution of the array is ∼ 0.7 ± 0.1° in the energy range from 30 TeV to 1 PeV, with a systematic error of ∼ 0°.
, the angular resolution of the array, as measured by the Moon and Sun shadowing technique, is 0.8° at 10 TeV, 0.7 ° at 100 TeV and 0.6 ° at 1 PeV.
the angular resolution of the EAS array is energy dependent, and the energy at which the angular resolution becomes 0.5° is ∼ 100  TeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GRAPES array is capable of detecting an isotropic flux of 10 ^{−13}  cm ^{−2}  s ^{−1} sr ^{−1} TeV ^{−1}, with an angular resolution of ∼ 1°, at energies of 30 TeV.
the GRAPES array has a very good energy-dependent angular resolution of ∼ 0.7–0.8° for energies in the range 10–300 TeV.
GRAPES- 3 has an angular resolution of ∼ 0.7 ° at energies as low > 30 TeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angular resolution of an EAS array, which has a high enough detector density, is not limited by the shower size, but by the detector size and the detector spacing.
a high density EAS array is capable of resolving the Moon shadow at TeV energies, and that such an array can be used as a tool to search for TeV point sources in the sky.
the Moon shadow can be observed in EAS data at a level of statistical significance of ∼ 10 σ and can be used for angular resolution studies.
